papers.title: Recurrent-Depth VLA: Test-Time Scaling
papers.summary: Achieves computational adaptivity via latent iterative refinement, enabling constant memory usage and up to 80x inference speedup over prior reasoning-based VLAs.

papers.title: SteerVLA: Steering VLAs in Long-Tail Driving
papers.summary: Leverages VLM reasoning to produce fine-grained language instructions that steer a VLA driving policy, significantly improving performance in long-tail scenarios.

papers.title: TwinRL-VLA: Digital Twin-Driven RL
papers.summary: A collaborative RL framework using high-fidelity digital twins to scale exploration for VLA models, achieving near 100% success in out-of-distribution regions.

papers.title: Contact-Anchored Policies (CAP)
papers.summary: Replaces language conditioning with physical contact points, outperforming state-of-the-art VLAs in zero-shot evaluations by 56%.

papers.title: Chi-Zero: Resource-Aware Robust Manipulation
papers.summary: A resource-efficient framework for high-reliability garment manipulation, capable of non-stop operation for 24 hours from arbitrary initial states.

papers.title: From Obstacles to Etiquette
papers.summary: Integrates geometric planning with fine-tuned VLM reasoning for social navigation, respecting human norms in complex environments.

papers.title: MOSAIC: Whole-Body Humanoid Teleoperation
papers.summary: Full-stack system for humanoid motion tracking and teleoperation using rapid residual adaptation to bridge the sim-to-real gap.

papers.title: SCALE: Self-Uncertainty for VLAs
papers.summary: A lightweight inference strategy using 'self-uncertainty' to modulate perception and action in VLA models without retraining.

papers.title: SD-VLA: Efficient Long-Horizon Control
papers.summary: Disentangles static and dynamic visual tokens to slash computational costs and improve long-horizon reasoning.

papers.title: DreamDojo: Robot World Model
papers.summary: A foundation world model pretrained on 44k hours of egocentric human videos, bridging the human-robot domain gap.
